subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core shell-facing admin notification broadcast surface now, fold it into the broader WebUI notification architecture, or keep shell-originated alerts outside core?
rationale: The requested feature is absent and useful, but it creates a new admin-scoped path from local shell scripts into visible UI interruptions, so authorization, payload, rate-limit, and product ownership cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Design Core Notify Contract
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical shell-to-Control-UI feature and require an explicit admin RPC/event, UI rendering, security, and abuse-control contract before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into WebUI Notifications
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20237 own the broader notification architecture only after it explicitly covers the CLI/admin Gateway surface requested here.

options.title: Prefer Plugin Or External Delivery
options.body: Decline a core command and document the supported plugin, channel, Web Push, or node-notify path if maintainers decide shell-originated alerts should not directly interrupt Control UI sessions.

recommendation.title: Design Core Notify Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical shell-to-Control-UI feature and require an explicit admin RPC/event, UI rendering, security, and abuse-control contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main blame and recent PR history place the central CLI/Gateway auth-scope boundary near this person’s recent work, making them the best routing candidate from the available evidence.
